summary: Bertie County, NC tower that a state lookout history dates to 1948 (120 ft); the 1959 survey gives 110 ft. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Square metal cabin on a four-legged steel structure

events.note: A 120-foot tower was erected by the State Forest Service, per the lookout history. The 1959 survey gives 110 ft overall; the sources disagree on height.
Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed and described the station: square metal cabin, 110 feet overall.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The survey datasheet spells the designation and village Rosemeade; the NC tower list and the brief use Rosemead. The coordinates match the survey position (36 10 57.97 N, 076 51 58.63 W), so both names refer to the same site.

sources.title: Survey data sheet for PID FX3886 (Rosemeade Lookout Tower)

notes_for_editor: Height conflict is unresolved: the 1948 history gives 120 ft erected; the 1959 survey gives 110 ft overall. The story reports both and does not pick one; neither source explains the gap. The 1948 date and agency come from the single compiled history page (Forest Lookouts). No source found describes the site or the tower today; the survey record has no condition note after 1959. Brief status and access stay unknown and are not set in facts. Web search budget was exhausted during this run, so only cached pages and direct page reads were used. Name spelling: the brief and the NC list say Rosemead; the NGS datasheet says Rosemeade.
